differences.title: 1. END-TO-END TYPE SAFETY
differences.leftDesc: tRPC generates TypeScript types from your server procedure definitions, ensuring compile-time safety for all API calls, eliminating runtime errors and enhancing developer confidence.
differences.rightDesc: GraphQL uses a schema definition language (SDL) to define types. While robust, it requires tools or manual effort to generate client-side types for full safety.

differences.title: 2. API CALL PATTERN
differences.leftDesc: tRPC abstracts your API into direct function calls, similar to local function invocations. This simplifies client-side code and leverages familiar programming patterns.
differences.rightDesc: GraphQL uses distinct query and mutation operations to fetch or modify data. This separation enforces a specific communication paradigm for clients.

differences.title: 3. OVER/UNDER-FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Since tRPC calls are type-safe and directly map to server procedures, you fetch exactly what the procedure returns, avoiding both over and under-fetching.
differences.rightDesc: GraphQL clients specify exactly which fields they need, preventing over-fetching. However, defining complex relationships can still lead to implicit under-fetching if not carefully modeled.

differences.title: 4. PROTOCOL TRANSPARENCY
differences.leftDesc: tRPC runs over standard HTTP or WebSockets. It hides the underlying transport, allowing seamless integration without requiring special client libraries for protocol handling.
differences.rightDesc: GraphQL typically operates over HTTP POST requests. While flexible, it relies on clients understanding the GraphQL query structure within the request body.

differences.title: 5. SCHEMA MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: tRPC's schema is derived from your server code. Changes in your server code automatically update the client-facing types, simplifying schema synchronization.
differences.rightDesc: GraphQL requires explicit schema definition and management. Changes necessitate updating the SDL and often regenerating client-side artifacts.

differences.title: 6. DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCE
differences.leftDesc: tRPC offers an unparalleled developer experience, feeling like you're calling local functions. Autocomplete and type checking work seamlessly across client and server.
differences.rightDesc: GraphQL provides a clear API contract via its schema. Tools like GraphiQL enhance exploration, but the experience is distinctly API-centric.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEXITY & BOILERPLATE
differences.leftDesc: tRPC minimizes boilerplate by inferring types and directly mapping server procedures. Setup is straightforward, especially within monorepos or full-stack frameworks.
differences.rightDesc: GraphQL can involve significant boilerplate for schema setup, resolvers, and client-side data fetching logic, especially when managing complex type relationships.
